name: TaxiDriver
author: Dominik
description: Stage 1 feasibility spike + Stage 2 visual swap + Stage 3 NPC driver ride (dev tool): spawn a vehicle (playerOwned=true), let an NPC take a seat, drive A to B autonomously via VehicleAgent.Navigate, and put the local player in and out of the car. Stage 2 swaps the visuals: vanilla Shitbox renderers/visual children are switched off (nothing destroyed) and assets/taxi.glb hangs in as a pure visual child of LandVehicle.vehicleModel via S1MAPI.Gltf.GltfLoader (layer + active-state normalised, colliders stripped, vanilla physics untouched). Stage 3: the vanilla NPC drives while the local player rides along - driver ride live-verified 2026-09-25 (seat proof: NPC root-to-seat distance 0.0m onto the isDriverSeat seat plus the LandVehicle.OccupantNPCs slot; callback result=Complete after 31.6s from the run 2 log that is still on disk, run 1 logged 14.5s and its log has since been pruned). Verified live 2026-09-25 after 13 rounds: callback result=Complete after 20.2 s to the road target (-131.4, -4.0, 51.9); the visual swap was verified live the same day (yellow boxy taxi instead of the Shitbox). Console command `taxi` is output-only (the MelonLoader console is log-only) - since 0.2.0 the taxi is ordered from the in-game phone via the built-in Taxi app (CALL TAXI + STOP button + live status label, the call-taxi flow is shared with the F5 hotkey in the single entry point SpikeCommands.CallTaxi); the F1-F12 hotkeys remain the diagnostic surface (remapped 2026-09-26: old F13-F17 -> F1-F5, the keyboard has only F1-F12), F4 toggles the visual swap for the next spawn, hotkeys only fire in the gameplay scene (menu scenes keep their own keys). Known limitations: VehicleSeat.isOccupied stays False for an NPC driver - isOccupied is Player-only (VehicleSeat.Occupant is typed Player), so NPC occupancy is proven by the LandVehicle.OccupantNPCs slot PLUS the measured root-to-seat distance, never by the seat flag; the OccupantNPCs[i] <-> Seats[i] index mapping is not directly observable in 0.4.7f6 and is verified for the single-driver case only (seating a second NPC to check OccupantNPCs[1] <-> Seats[1] is open); ~8.3 m end tolerance with endAtRoad=true (arrival threshold 10 m); GLB wheels do not rotate. Stage 3d (2026-09-27): the ride destination is no longer a hand-read coordinate — `taxi pois` dumps every place the GAME owns (live DeliveryLocation instances incl. their TeleportPoint, plus every ParkingLot's street-side entry) and the Taxi app lists them as tappable rows (deal locations first, then lots, plus the proven taxi stand). The arrival rule decides where the taxi actually stops: goal on the vehicle graph -> drive it directly; otherwise the nearest lot entry within 60 m -> drop off beside it; otherwise refuse instead of force-driving into geometry (the taxi never teleports to the graph any more: teleportToGraphIfCalculationFails=false, and the forced pre-dispatch orientation snap is gone). STOP now despawns the taxi (proven cleanup order: everyone verified out, then StopNavigating, then DestroyVehicle; a failed exit refuses the destroy), because the old 'navigation off, player left seated' behaviour read as 'the game is stuck' while the NPC held the driver seat. A progress watchdog measures movement instead of trusting AutoDriving (observed 2026-09-27: AutoDriving=True, navCalc=False, speed 0.0 km/h for 9.6 s) and runs a recovery ladder: reverse 1.5 s then re-dispatch, then fall back to another lot entry near the goal, then give up with an actionable message. A 1 s ride heartbeat ([hb]) tells a real main-thread hang apart from a stuck state. Stage 4 (2026-09-27): "können wir nicht die KI klonen, vom Spiel z.B. die wo das Polizeifahrzeug steuert" — the taxi no longer drives on the mod's own dispatch call. TaxiAI builds a VehiclePatrolRoute at runtime (two waypoints: where the car is, where it should be), attaches the game's own VehiclePatrolBehaviour to the taxi driver and starts it — the same supervisor that drives the police car, with its own progression threshold, pathing-failure counter and IsAsCloseAsPossible arrival rule. The mod only supervises: arrival verdict, stall detection, timeout. A stall does not fight the behaviour, it releases it and falls back to the proven Navigate() dispatch, so a broken clone degrades instead of freezing. The game's MAX_CONSECUTIVE_PATHING_FAILURES is adopted as the mod's re-dispatch budget; every supervision number (patrol + pursuit) is dumped live on the first ride (`taxi ai` exists but the MelonLoader console is log-only). 0.5.1 (2026-09-28): the destination list is legible — measured from Dominik's screenshot (app canvas 655x1201 units at 0.42 px/unit, so Sp(11) was 5 px of text, while the Weather app he accepts uses 8 px minimum / 13 px rows). Rows are Dp(48) with Sp(18) bold text, the 'DEAL * ' prefix became a small right-aligned tag, all other text grew (header Sp(22), CALL TAXI Sp(20), STOP Sp(18)), and the list panel is Dp(370) tall so the previously empty lower quarter of the screen is used. 0.5.2 (2026-09-28): nothing in the app can be cut off any more — row names, the tag column, the destination line and the place counter are single-line rects with uGUI best-fit (font shrinks between Sp(18) and Sp(12) instead of wrapping out of its row or running past the app container), and the app now measures its own labels: the [ui] log line reports the name column width, the font sizes and the widest place names with their needed width, so the fit is checked by measurement instead of by eye. 0.5.3 (2026-09-28): fixed the app's own layout bug that clipped the first letters of every row (rows/header/counter now use HorizontalLayoutGroup children like the BankApp instead of hand-placed rects, whose boxes sat left of the row and were cut by the scroll mask), and the row tag now switches colour with the selection (grey on bright yellow was unreadable), and fixed the [ui] measurement to report with the scale the app was BUILT with (the theme scale is global and changes with the last app opened).
